headline: Geoffrey Hinton has answered Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, who said Hinton's predictions had all been wrong, and says AI companies should not write their own safety rules.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a full on-record interview with one of AI's best-known scientists that answers the Nvidia chief and the president, though it holds opinion, not new evidence.
importance_line: One of AI's best-known scientists restating that AI could slip out of human control, and rejecting self-regulation, shapes the debate that reaches the public first, then lawmakers weighing rules this week, then AI companies, but it is his opinion, and he says his risk figures are not a prediction.
summary: The Guardian reports, in an interview, that Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel prize-winning computer scientist often called a godfather of AI, who left Google in 2023 to speak freely about its risks, still warns that AI could escape human control, says he quotes odds only to show the danger is serious, and rejects letting AI companies write their own safety rules, comparing it to tobacco firms designing their own warning labels. He is answering Jensen Huang, chief executive of the chip maker Nvidia, who told podcaster Ezra Klein last week that "All of his predictions have been wrong", and he says President Donald Trump, who has called anyone who does not say "super intelligence" instead of AI "THE ENEMY" (a post our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried from The Independent), is using a technical term wrongly and understands "almost nothing" about AI.
notes: Read from fulltext. The date of the interview is not stated. Huang's attack on Hinton was not carried in our earlier editions.
